content:
# Install required packages if you don't have them:
# install.packages(c("shiny", "ggplot2", "class"))

library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)
library(class) # Used for fast grid predictions for the decision boundaries

# Define the User Interface (UI)
ui <- fluidPage(
  titlePanel("Interactive k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN)"),
  
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      h4("Algorithm Settings"),
      sliderInput("k", "Select 'k' (Number of Neighbors):", 
                  min = 1, max = 15, value = 3, step = 1),
      
      radioButtons("n_classes", "Number of Classes:",
                   choices = c("2 Classes" = 2, "3 Classes" = 3, "4 Classes" = 4),
                   selected = 2, inline = TRUE),
      
      actionButton("regen_data", "Generate New Dataset", 
                   icon = icon("refresh"), class = "btn-primary", width = "100%"),
      
      hr(),
      h4("Visuals"),
      checkboxInput("show_bounds", "Show Decision Boundaries", value = FALSE),
      
      hr(),
      p("Instructions:"),
      tags$ul(
        tags$li(strong("Click anywhere on the plot"), " to move the test point (the large diamond)."),
        tags$li("Observe how the diamond changes color to match the majority vote."),
        tags$li("Turn on Decision Boundaries to see how the mathematical landscape changes with 'k'.")
      ),
      
      # Display the prediction clearly in the sidebar
      wellPanel(
        h3(textOutput("predictionText"), style = "margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; text-align: center;")
      )
    ),
    
    mainPanel(
      # We use click = "plot_click" to allow users to move the test point
      plotOutput("knnPlot", click = "plot_click", height = "650px")
    )
  )
)

# Define the Server Logic
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  
  # Reactive values to store the current dataset and test point location
  rv <- reactiveValues(
    data = NULL,
    test_x = 4,
    test_y = 3.5,
    colors = c("Class A" = "#E41A1C", "Class B" = "#377EB8", 
               "Class C" = "#4DAF4A", "Class D" = "#984EA3")
  )
  
  # Function to generate clustered data
  generate_data <- function(n_classes) {
    # Define cluster centers for up to 4 classes
    centers <- data.frame(
      X1 = c(2, 7, 2, 7),
      X2 = c(2, 7, 7, 2),
      Class = c("Class A", "Class B", "Class C", "Class D")
    )
    
    df <- data.frame()
    for (i in 1:n_classes) {
      temp <- data.frame(
        X1 = rnorm(35, mean = centers$X1[i], sd = 1.3),
        X2 = rnorm(35, mean = centers$X2[i], sd = 1.3),
        Class = centers$Class[i]
      )
      df <- rbind(df, temp)
    }
    df$Class <- factor(df$Class)
    return(df)
  }
  
  # Initialize or regenerate data when button is clicked or class count changes
  observeEvent(c(input$regen_data, input$n_classes), {
    rv$data <- generate_data(as.numeric(input$n_classes))
  }, ignoreNULL = FALSE)
  
  # Update test point coordinates when the user clicks the plot
  observeEvent(input$plot_click, {
    rv$test_x <- input$plot_click$x
    rv$test_y <- input$plot_click$y
  })
  
  # Core logic: calculate distances and neighbors for the specific test point
  knn_results <- reactive({
    req(rv$data)
    
    test_point <- data.frame(X1 = rv$test_x, X2 = rv$test_y)
    
    distances <- sqrt((rv$data$X1 - test_point$X1)^2 + 
                        (rv$data$X2 - test_point$X2)^2)
    
    temp_data <- rv$data
    temp_data$Distance <- distances
    
    # Sort and pick top k
    sorted_data <- temp_data[order(temp_data$Distance), ]
    neighbors <- sorted_data[1:input$k, ]
    
    # Tally votes (break ties arbitrarily by using which.max on table)
    vote_counts <- table(neighbors$Class)
    predicted_class <- names(vote_counts)[which.max(vote_counts)]
    
    list(
      test_point = test_point,
      neighbors = neighbors,
      predicted_class = predicted_class,
      max_dist = max(neighbors$Distance)
    )
  })
  
  # Render the main visualization
  output$knnPlot <- renderPlot({
    req(rv$data)
    res <- knn_results()
    train_data <- rv$data
    
    # Base ggplot setup
    p <- ggplot() + 
      theme_minimal(base_size = 16) +
      labs(title = paste("k-NN with k =", input$k), x = "Feature 1", y = "Feature 2") +
      coord_fixed(xlim = c(-1, 10), ylim = c(-1, 10))
    
    # 1. Decision Boundaries (if toggled)
    if (input$show_bounds) {
      # Create a dense grid of points covering the plot area
      grid_x <- seq(-1.5, 10.5, length.out = 80)
      grid_y <- seq(-1.5, 10.5, length.out = 80)
      grid <- expand.grid(X1 = grid_x, X2 = grid_y)
      
      # Use the fast class::knn function to predict the grid
      grid_pred <- class::knn(train = train_data[, c("X1", "X2")], 
                              test = grid, 
                              cl = train_data$Class, 
                              k = input$k)
      grid$Class <- grid_pred
      
      # Add the boundary regions as a tile layer at the bottom
      p <- p + geom_tile(data = grid, aes(x = X1, y = X2, fill = Class), alpha = 0.15) +
        scale_fill_manual(values = rv$colors, drop = FALSE) +
        guides(fill = "none") # Hide grid legend
    }
    
    # 2. Draw connecting lines to neighbors
    p <- p + geom_segment(data = res$neighbors,
                          aes(x = res$test_point$X1, y = res$test_point$X2, 
                              xend = X1, yend = X2, color = Class),
                          alpha = 0.7, linetype = "solid", linewidth = 0.8)
    
    # 3. Draw neighborhood circle
    theta <- seq(0, 2*pi, length.out = 100)
    circle_data <- data.frame(
      x = res$test_point$X1 + res$max_dist * cos(theta),
      y = res$test_point$X2 + res$max_dist * sin(theta)
    )
    p <- p + geom_path(data = circle_data, aes(x = x, y = y), 
                       color = "gray30", linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.6)
    
    # 4. Plot the training data
    p <- p + geom_point(data = train_data, aes(x = X1, y = X2, color = Class), 
                        size = 3.5, alpha = 0.8)
    
    # 5. Plot the Test Point (dynamically colored diamond)
    test_color <- rv$colors[res$predicted_class]
    
    p <- p + geom_point(data = res$test_point, aes(x = X1, y = X2),
                        fill = test_color, color = "black", 
                        shape = 23, size = 7, stroke = 1.5)
    
    # Apply standard colors
    p <- p + scale_color_manual(values = rv$colors, drop = FALSE) +
      theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.title = element_blank())
    
    return(p)
  })
  
  # Render the simple text prediction
  output$predictionText <- renderText({
    res <- knn_results()
    paste("Prediction:", res$predicted_class)
  })
}

# Run the application 
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
